one_month_reasoning: The window contains Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-15 after the close. I expect a sequentially weaker quarter than Q2's $901M adjusted EBITDA: Q3 LME averaged below Q2's spike to $3,855/t, and the US Midwest premium dropped about 8% to 95c/lb in mid-August on the proposed cut to tariffs on Canadian metal. Management had guided the alumina segment about $10M better and aluminum about flat, and the stock is already down 50% from its high and about 18% since Sept 2 ($51.05), so a lot of this looks priced in. Other drivers in the window: China restocking after National Day (Shanghai ingot inventories fell sharply, which is supportive), the October Fed decision (rate-hike odds near 50-50, bearish for the dollar-commodity trade), any South32 shareholder vote or regulatory step, and Iran/Hormuz headlines (Polymarket puts Hormuz normal by Dec 31 at only 20%). LME aluminium broke its moving averages on Sept 29, a mild negative momentum signal; this is offset by cheap valuation and possible short covering. With no strong directional edge, I centre near $42.2 with monthly vol of about 16.5% (56%/3.5, rounded up slightly for the earnings event).

fair_value.method: Pro forma for the South32 aluminium assets (about 281M shares, about $5.4B adjusted net debt): 2027E EBITDA of about $3.5B at LME about $2,950/t x 5.0x EV/EBITDA gives about $43, plus about $0.8B of retained FCF by Sept 2027, giving $46. A cross-check of 2027E EPS of about $5.6 x 8x gives $45. Blended: $45.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E combined EBITDA $3.5B (Alcoa standalone about $2.6B + AliGroup about $0.9B) x 5.0x = EV $17.5B; less pro forma adjusted net debt about $5.4B = $12.1B; plus about $0.8B 12-month FCF = $12.9B; / 281M shares = about $46

inputs_detail.input: Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA (run-rate anchor at peak prices)

inputs_detail.derivation: Midpoint of the 2027 forecasts cited by trade press: Morgan Stanley $2,850, Goldman $2,750 (fast Gulf restart) to $3,250 (slow restart), others $2,750-3,075. I lean slightly above the midpoint because Hormuz is still not normal (source 11).

Q2 2026 annualized $3.6B at about $3,500/t LME and a record Midwest premium. Haircut by about $200M per $100/t for the about $550/t lower LME, and about $0.2B for a lower Midwest premium (source 7). Partly offset by lower Canadian tariff costs.
FY2025 pro forma pre-tax $502M + D&A $303M + interest $143M = about $950M (from Alcoa's pro forma filing). Held roughly flat for 2027 on lower aluminium partly offset by Worsley volume recovery.

Mid-cycle multiple for a commodity smelter-refiner facing a forecast 2027 surplus. Today's implied multiple on H1 2026 pro forma EBITDA (about $3.8B annualized from source 2) is about 4.4x on peak-ish earnings.

Pro forma June 30 2026 debt $5.39B less cash $0.67B = $4.72B, plus pension/OPEB of about $0.65B (Alcoa's adjusted net debt convention). Excludes the up-to-$750M CVR, which is unlikely to pay at 2027 forecast prices.
Q2 2026 FCF was $422M at peak prices. I assume about $200M per quarter at lower 2027 prices, net of interest on the new 6.6-6.9% notes.

EBITDA $3.5B - D&A about $1.0B (FY25 pro forma $916M) - interest about $0.4B (pro forma $395M) = $2.1B pretax; tax 25% gives $1.57B; / 281M shares = $5.6. For comparison, H1 2026 pro forma EPS was $3.64 at peak prices.
Trough-to-mid-cycle P/E for aluminium producers when the market expects a shift from deficit to surplus.

bear.story: Gulf smelters (EGA full by Q1 2027) and Bahrain restart quickly, Hormuz normalizes, and Indonesia and China overproduce. The 2027 surplus reaches 1-2Mt, LME falls to about $2,600, and the Midwest premium compresses further with Canadian tariff relief. Alcoa EBITDA drops to about $2.2B on a heavier debt load after the South32 deal, plus integration and Pinjarra issues.

base.story: LME averages about $2,900-3,000 in 2027 and the South32 assets close and integrate. The stock re-rates modestly from 4.4x toward 5x mid-cycle EBITDA as FCF delevers the balance sheet.

bull.story: Iran conflict and Hormuz stay disrupted (Polymarket: Hormuz normal by end-2026 only 20%), Gulf restarts slip into late 2027, and China stays at its cap. LME holds $3,400+ and the Midwest premium stays near $1/lb. Combined EBITDA of $4.5B+ and deal synergies push the stock back toward its 2026 highs.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $27 (well under the 52-week low of $31.45), the stock would imply EV/EBITDA under about 3.5x even on a $2,800 LME. That would most likely mean a structural problem: an aluminium price collapse toward $2,500 from a large 2027 surplus, a failed or value-destroying South32 integration, or a balance-sheet strain from the new $2.6B of notes. Ordinary volatility would not explain it.

reasoning: AA spiked to $84 in Q2 2026 when Iranian strikes knocked out about 2Mt/yr of Gulf aluminium (EGA, Alba, Qatalum) and LME hit $3,855/t on June 2. It has since round-tripped to $42 on several things: peace and restart hopes, an EGA restart running ahead of schedule (full by Q1 2027), the lower Midwest premium after the Canadian tariff cut, a Q2 EPS miss ($2.12 vs $2.32), lower alumina guidance after the Pinjarra cyclone and oxalate problems, and the dilutive South32 acquisition ($3.1B cash + 17M shares, financed by $2.6B of 6.6-6.9% notes). On pro forma numbers the stock looks optically cheap at about 4.4x annualized H1 EBITDA and about 6x H1 EPS. But those are peak-price earnings, and the trade-press consensus (MS, GS, BofA) sees 2027 swinging into a 0.8-1.5Mt surplus with LME at $2,750-3,075. Normalizing to about $2,950 LME gives a fair value of about $45 (EV/EBITDA 5x, with a P/E cross-check), only modestly above $42. Alternative signals cut both ways. Polymarket still prices only 20% for Hormuz normal by end-2026 and 13% for a nuclear deal (upside tail for prices). The September 29 technical breakdown, fresh short accumulation and Fed-hike odds are bearish near-term. China's sharp pre-holiday ingot destock is supportive. With realized vol of 56%, I used a lognormal centred on about $43.5 (a slight positive drift toward fair value) with sigma 0.50, and kept a slightly fatter lower tail for the debt and surplus risks. Research was limited: Twelve Data estimates and earnings endpoints were not available on the plan, I found no reachable Reddit or X threads, and the mining.com article returned 403.
